recap.text: Mordecai names the thing the Iron Tangle caricatures as the Apothecary. She is a collective mind who synthesises elements and is spreading, which makes people elsewhere nervous.

The Apothecary fills the last sponsorship slot. A spokeswoman in a brown cloak patterned with circles and lines tells a stagehand not to cut Carl off, and the stagehand freezes. The Apothecary and the Plenty both send protection against vampirism on the same day. The Apothecary sends five boxes to different crawlers for Princess Donut, including a tiara and an Enchanted Hammer of Fast Forward. Katia receives a beanie that sinks into her.

Agatha's feed carries the chatter of the Apothecary. Thousands of agents are seeded across the planet and ordered to kill themselves if they miss the dungeon. These agents recite a daily mantra of inaccuracies and half-truths to secretly implant a hidden upgrade in crawlers.

The Apothecary sends Donut a platinum benefactor box containing a purple charging pillow. It drains magical items for ten hours and transfers buffs only to absorption crystals on like items. The AI asks Carl, Orren, and Donut for advice using a metaphor about two women who want a man in prison dead. Donut tells the AI to determine if the man is good or bad and to stay out of it.

The AI explains that the Primals became a collective to stop warring and waste. The Apothecary was engineered to meld into the collective but joined the resistance. When the collective launched a nine-tier attack against biological life, the Apothecary stood in front of it.

beats.headline: The truer translation
beats.text: Mordecai puts a name to the thing the Iron Tangle keeps caricaturing. Apothecary is the closer translation, taken from her ability to synthesise elements, and the dungeon's version bends the joke into an insult. She is a collective mind and she is spreading, which is a sentence that makes a great many people elsewhere nervous.
beats.gist: Mordecai names the Collective mind the Apothecary, a spreading entity that makes people elsewhere nervous.

beats.headline: The third and final sponsor
beats.text: Clint has the account of Scolopendra's attack, and says the high elves were protected by something they had stolen. On the way back to Point Mongo the last sponsorship slot fills. The Apothecary takes it.
beats.gist: The Apothecary fills the last sponsorship slot while Clint and others return to Point Mongo.

beats.headline: Their spokeswoman takes the floor
beats.text: A woman in a brown cloak patterned with circles and lines tells the stagehand not to cut Carl off, and he freezes. The people nearest her get up and move away. She cannot address Carl directly, she says, because she is one of his sponsors and it would breach the contract; she is also a sponsor of CrawlCon, and she has told them to let him speak. Then she walks out, and Circe Took calls her a bitch. Uptown Hal names her afterwards: the collective's spokeswoman.
beats.gist: A woman in a brown cloak tells a stagehand not to cut Carl off.

beats.headline: The same gift, the same day
beats.text: She and the Plenty each send protection against vampirism, and the two parcels arrive together. Sponsors are not supposed to coordinate. Carl now has two who do.
beats.gist: The Apothecary and the Plenty send protection against vampirism, and the two parcels arrive together.

beats.headline: Their boxes are for the cat
beats.text: Minutes after Prepotente delivers a potion his sponsor meant for Princess Donut, Elle announces a benefactor box from the Apothecary, and Imani messages that she has one as well. Imani has opened hers. It is also for Donut. Donut, meanwhile, decides out loud that Carl's nipple-ring bribe was a trick, and that he was directed to give her that earlier potion all along.
beats.gist: Prepotente delivers a potion to Donut; Elle and Imani announce benefactor boxes from the Apothecary for Donut.

beats.headline: Five boxes, all for the cat
beats.text: Five items on the table, all Apothecary sponsor boxes, each sent to a different crawler with a note saying it belongs to Princess Donut: a wand recharge scroll, a tiara, sheet music, an Enchanted Hammer of Fast Forward that Borant tried and failed to block with an appeal, and an enchanted metal stick, named for someone Mordecai cannot place, given to Dmitri Popov. The hammer does nothing magical; the stick is no wand, but used correctly it can do something truly magical. Each carries a small seven worked into it. The one Apothecary box not meant for Donut went to Katia: a beanie that sank into her.
beats.gist: The Apothecary sends five sponsor boxes to crawlers, all belonging to Princess Donut.

beats.headline: A mantra with mistakes in it
beats.text: Agatha's feed carries the Apothecary's chatter as well as her own team's. Thousands of its agents are seeded across the planet, ordered to kill themselves if they miss the dungeon. This season they mean to contact crawlers directly, in the dungeon or on the floor with the memory ghosts, and for months they have made their agents recite a daily mantra full of known inaccuracies and half-truths. The errors are there to keep the crawler alive around the showrunners. What the mantra really does is secretly implant a hidden upgrade.
beats.gist: Agatha's feed carries the Apothecary's chatter. Its agents recite a mantra of inaccuracies to implant upgrades.

beats.headline: A second pillow
beats.text: A platinum benefactor box arrives for Donut from the Apothecary in the same sitting as the tiara, and it holds a second charging pillow, purple where the first is red. The same ten-hour drain, and the same ruin after one hour. The difference is at the end of the description: this one drains any magical item, but transfers only to an absorption crystal on a like item. A ring's buff goes to a ring; sent to the wrong kind of item, the buff is lost. With two pillows, the tiara fills twice as fast.
beats.gist: Donut receives a purple charging pillow from the Apothecary that drains magical items into absorption crystals.

beats.headline: The AI asks which side to take
beats.text: It wants advice from Orren and from Carl, and teleports Donut in as well, and it asks in a laboured metaphor about relationships: a girlfriend who looks like Agatha, and an older woman who has been giving it pointers on getting stronger, both of whom want the same man in prison dead. Donut tells it to find out whether he is really good or really bad before doing anything, and even then to stay out of it unless it has no choice.
beats.gist: The AI asks Orren and Carl for advice and teleports Donut into a laboured metaphor.

beats.headline: The whole of it, on stage
beats.text: The AI gives the account itself. The Primals were individuals once, and their society spread until the warring and the waste made them decide to end it and keep their minds in one collective instead. Those who refused fled. The Apothecary was born near the end, engineered to meld into the whole, and joined the resistance instead. The collective became a weapon aimed at every remaining scrap of biological life, and when it let off the nine-tier attack she stood in front of it, and what grew back afterwards grew back behind her.
beats.gist: The AI explains the Collective mind and how the Apothecary protected biological life from a nine-tier attack.
